title: Nuclear power is too dangerous for Australia, as Chernobyl and Fukushima show
oneLiner: Two major accidents are offered as reason enough to keep the ban.
body: The two most serious nuclear accidents displaced hundreds of thousands of people and left land unusable for decades. Proponents of the ban argue that no economic case justifies exposing Australian communities to that category of risk.
contextBackground: Safety is the oldest argument against nuclear power and the one most often made in public, though rarely by energy specialists on either side. It is included here because it is widely held, and so the community's rating of it is informative.
contextDisagreement: Opponents of this claim argue that reactor designs, regulation and siting have changed substantially since both accidents, and that per unit of electricity nuclear has a lower death toll than coal or gas. The claim as written does not engage with that comparison.

otherClaim.title: Australia should repeal its federal ban on nuclear power generation

claimItself.title: Australia should repeal its federal ban on nuclear power generation
claimItself.oneLiner: Whether the 1998 prohibition on nuclear power plants should be lifted. Repeal is a separate question from whether anyone would then build one.
claimItself.body: Two federal Acts prohibit the approval of a nuclear power plant anywhere in Australia. Repealing them would allow proposals to be assessed on their merits under the ordinary environmental, safety and planning regimes. Whether a plant would then be commercially viable, or built in time to matter, is argued below.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: CSIRO's GenCost report finds firmed renewables the cheapest new-build electricity for Australia and large-scale nuclear the most expensive

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Nuclear power cannot help with Australia's electricity prices or reliability in time to matter

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: The political fight over nuclear is distracting from solving price and emissions problems now
